speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) in each of the last three years, what is the number of complaints made in relation to defects in HDB BTO flats within five years of their completion; (b) what is this figure as a percentage of the total number of HDB BTO flats completed in that year; and (c) whether HBD will consider extending the defects liability period with its contractors for a longer period of up to five years to ensure greater responsibility for workmanship.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The vast majority of reported defects involve issues such as scratches or cracks on timber surfaces, walls, tiles and sanitary fittings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These are easily rectified by the contractors and do not affect the structural integrity or safety of the building.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As most defects are resolved within the first year, a one-year DLP is sufficient for the majority of new flat owners and is in line with the industry practice for private developments.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But in certain BTOs I have had in my estate, Woodland Glen is one of them.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: There are about 888 units and we have had more than 200 complaints so far on defects; most of which HDB is trying to rectify but HDB has no recourse against the original developer legally.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, I was just wondering whether HDB or MND has a way of keeping track of maybe individual developers that have significant issues like this, where more than a quarter of the units will have defects that have come up later.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And these are not things to do with wear and tear; it is like windows panes melting, toilet seats breaking.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, it just sounds like quality is bad or workmanship is bad.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I had earlier omitted in my answer to also mention that if any maintenance issues are reported after the DLP, HDB will investigate the likely cause and advise flat owners on the follow-up action accordingly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if the issue is assessed to be due to an inherent defect or quality issue, HDB will engage the building contractor to rectify it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Member raised the question of what happens when you have certain developments that may have more than the usual number of defects.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I think he referred in particular to Woodlands Glen.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The BTO project at Woodlands Glen consists of five residential blocks with a total of 888 units and the flats in the MSCP were completed between March 2017 and June 2017.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I think that a number of the residents had appealed to Mr Nair with regard to the defects.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they agreed to replace that – the bumpers and the window weather seal, upon the residents' feedback.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And with regard to the other reported defects, for example, there was feedback about rusty gate and timber toilet door issues, HDB followed up to resolve the issues with the residents.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, HDB is working closely with the contractor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In short therefore, I think the position is this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On DLP specifically and the length of it, the numbers show that one year would be sufficient because the vast majority of the defects appear within that period and those are generally fairly minor defects.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have provisions obviously for major things like wall seepage and spalling concrete.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when you do have outliers like this, HDB will work closely with the contractor to rectify the defects and to see how they can be made good because obviously people moving into new BTOs would want their premises to be nice to live in.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And it is obviously upsetting when there are defects, because they mar your enjoyment of the premises.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, will HDB continue to act on these defects until they are fully resolved?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: My second question – several residents in DBSS development in my constituency have reported a large number of similar defects soon after the DLP.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What options are available to lessees who encounter defects after the DLP and will HDB consider co-payment arrangements, so that lessees do not have to bear the full cost of rectifications on their own?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to the first question, if the defects are reported within the DLP, then obviously, it is within the relevant time frame and they should be followed up upon.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the defects which come up after the DLP period, as mentioned earlier, HDB will investigate the cause and then decide on what the best course of action is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The reason I say this – and I sort of cannot give a definitive answer that yes, automatically everything after the defects liability period will be attended to by HDB – is because it depends on the nature of the defect.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It depends on what exactly the cause is and it also depends on the nature of the follow-up action that needs to be taken.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think the the assurance we can give is this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If there is a problem after the defects liability period, HDB will look into it and do its best to resolve it with the contractor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But obviously if it is something that crops up 10 years later, then that is a very different thing.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In cases where the residents have encountered multiple repair attempts to water seepage and wall seepage problems due to shoddy waterproofing works done by the contractor, and despite multiple attempts by contractors to fix the same problem, the problem keeps coming back in intervals of two to three years for the past 10-15 years – what recourse do residents have from HDB in terms of the distress that they have had to live through for the many years in encountering these problems?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Again, it goes back to a question of identifying the source or the cause of the problem.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if it falls within the five-year warranty, it will be dealt with on the basis of that warranty.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But if the seepage arose, let us say, maybe in the sixth year and it was because of the unit above having done certain renovation works and therefore broken the waterproofing or done something, then, it really would not be correct to look to HDB for that because the owner above will also have to bear some responsibility.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, it goes back to the approach that I said earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We would look at the cause, we would look at where the fault is or what the reason is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The residents will point to leakage, they think it comes from a certain place but actually it may come from somewhere else.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You have got to trace it, you have got to find the cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And whoever is responsible for having generated that cause or made that leakage happen, should generally be the one to deal with it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But bearing in mind that for flats – and this is the same for HDB as well as for private developments – there is a defects liability period or DLP for a reason and there is a warranty period for a reason.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the assurance you have is that they will be investigated and dealt with accordingly.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Does the HDB monitor the extent of BTO flat defects associated with particular contractors in particular developments?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And is that information then, given consideration in the decision-making process to award future contracts to that particular contractor?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if the Member could just file a question on that, then we will be able to get back to him.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For the defect liability period for both BTO and HIP projects, given the length of time of the circuit breaker and shortage in workers, will the Ministry consider an automatic six-month extension or some suitable period for the defect liability periods that have expired within this time frame?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Can I just clarify with the Member, before she goes back to her seat.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because the defects liability period usually runs from a certain time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if the works have not been completed yet, the defects liability period does not run.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I just wanted to clarify what time period she meant?
